newsitem.title: ITALY: Hard left warns Italy's Prodi off confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Hard left warns Italy's Prodi off confidence vote.

text.p: The hard-left Communist Refoundation party said on Monday it would not back the government if it decided to put the question of sending an Italian-led security force to Albania to a confidence vote.
On a confidence vote, a government is obliged to resign if it loses.

Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti, whose party assures Prime Minister Romano Prodi of a parliamentary majority, made the position clear after Refoundation's leadership reaffirmed its opposition to the Albania mission.
Deployment of the force, which is backed by the opposition, goes to votes in the two houses of parliament on Tuesday and Wednesday. The votes will be on simple resolutions.

Media speculation has mounted that Prodi could make the issue a confidence test to try to swing Refoundation into line but the prime minister told the daily La Repubblica on Monday that he had not yet considered the option.

"Naturally since we are against the mission, if the government presumed to put the military mission to a confidence test we would vote against because it's what we are against. But it (a confidence vote) would be totally arbitrary," Bertinotti said.
